description: Every way of authenticating that AgentFrontier understands. A source definition lists the method ids it supports and, per protocol, how each method's fields map onto the driver or the HTTP request. Fields of type `secret` and `secret_text` are never logged and must be stored encrypted. `provider` names code that derives extra values at connect time (for example an OAuth access token); `static` means the fields are used as given.

methods.name: No authentication
methods.description: Open source, or authenticated by the network (VPN, private link, local file).

methods.name: Username only (no password)
methods.description: Trust, peer or ident logins and local development databases.

methods.name: Username and password
methods.description: Classic database login; HTTP sources send it as Basic authentication.

methods.name: Access token / personal access token
methods.description: Bearer token, PAT or programmatic access token. Database sources usually send it in place of the password (RDS IAM, Entra ID tokens).

fields.label: Username
fields.help: Only if the source pairs the token with a user.

methods.name: API key
methods.description: Static key for SaaS and HTTP APIs, sent in a header or a query parameter.

fields.label: Header name
fields.help: Overrides the header the source definition uses by default.

fields.label: Key id
fields.help: For sources whose keys come as an id plus a secret.

methods.name: Key pair (private key)
methods.description: RSA key pair authentication, for example Snowflake service users.

methods.name: OAuth 2.0 client credentials
methods.description: Machine-to-machine OAuth: the SDK fetches and refreshes the access token itself.

fields.label: Token URL
fields.help: Leave empty to use the source definition's default endpoint.

methods.name: OAuth 2.0 refresh token
methods.description: A user-delegated grant (authorization code flow done once, elsewhere); the SDK exchanges the refresh token for access tokens.

methods.name: OAuth 2.0 access token
methods.description: A pre-issued, short-lived OAuth access token.

methods.name: AWS IAM
methods.description: Access keys, optionally assuming a role (S3, Redshift, Athena, Glue, RDS IAM).

fields.label: Access key ID
fields.help: Empty to use the default credential chain.

methods.name: Azure service principal
methods.description: Entra ID app registration (ADLS, Synapse, Azure SQL, Microsoft Graph for OneDrive and SharePoint).

methods.name: Azure managed identity
methods.description: The identity of the Azure resource the SDK runs on.

methods.name: Entra ID user and password
methods.description: Entra ID (Azure AD) user login, for example to Azure SQL or Synapse.

methods.name: GCP service account
methods.description: Service account key JSON (BigQuery, GCS, Cloud SQL).

fields.label: Project ID
fields.help: Defaults to the project in the key.

methods.name: Client certificate (mTLS)
methods.description: TLS client certificate authentication.

methods.name: Kerberos
methods.description: GSSAPI / Kerberos (Hadoop, Hive, enterprise databases).

methods.name: Windows integrated / NTLM
methods.description: Windows authentication (SQL Server). Empty username uses the identity of the running process.

methods.name: Connection string
methods.description: A complete connection string or JDBC URL that already carries the credentials.

methods.name: SSH key
methods.description: SFTP and SSH based file systems.

methods.name: Custom
methods.description: Free-form fields whose meaning the source definition decides. Every value is treated as a secret.
